mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than the baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which can lead to economic downturns and negative equity returns. If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5 percentage points, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in >40% of cases when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with increasing housing starts indicates a robust economy, which should drive positive equity returns. This mechanism requires both GDPC1 growth >2% and HOUST >1850.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative when both GDPC1 growth >2% and HOUST >1850, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production during a late-cycle expansion signals potential supply chain issues, leading to negative equity returns. This mechanism is active when INDPRO growth turns negative.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO growth is negative in a late-cycle expansion, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Consistent job growth, as indicated by increasing PAYEMS, signals a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC for PAYEMS and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in real personal consumption expenditure (RSAFS) growth below 0.2% per month indicates weakening demand, which should lead to negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when RSAFS growth <0.2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates coupled with increasing unemployment rates signal monetary tightening and labor market weakness, leading to negative equity returns. This mechanism requires both FEDFUNDS >3% and UNRATE >5%.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive when both FEDFUNDS >3% and UNRATE >5%, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an early-cycle expansion signals recovering demand, which should drive positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative when HOUST >1800 in an early-cycle expansion, this hypothesis is rejected.
